<!-- pr-reviewer: b851ef625e9ea3cd50c01c406ef62ec617692775 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (safety floor: re-review of the narrowed excuse; the earlier blocker is closed, no new blocker found).

**What looks good**
- The shortfall rows of the first review are fixed. A hidden floor is now excused only when it is out of the nose's reach AND no path segment stands level with its recess (`scan_turned.rs` `excuses`, called from `scan_hidden.rs` `judge_rows`). Any doubt (spindle not along Z, no roof, non-finite station) means no excuse, so the verdict refuses and never passes.
- The rule only narrows the old one, and it is a refusal-direction change: it can add a conviction, never remove one.
- I tried to break it myself on the issue's groove bar (r10, groove r5.5 over z34..37, spindle Z, leave 0), centre z / centre r:
  - 35.5 / 6.3 and 36.0 / 6.3: convict (the pinned rows).
  - OD ride into the mouth span (to z 37.5): rest 4.94, convicts.
  - Ride past the groove without entering (to z 30): rest 3.75, convicts.
  - Pass below the floor (z 33): convicts.
  - Wider nose (1.2): shortfall radially 1.17 and near-wall 0.99 convict (my fixture also gouged 0.4 there, which only refuses more).
  - The one thing that still posts clean is a pass that never reaches the groove's axial span at all, e.g. an OD ride that ends at z 37.9 (nose bottom 37.1, mouth at 37). That is the facing case by design: a groove no segment came near is another operation's. It is the same blind spot as bulk stock on the shaft, pre-existing and out of this PR's scope (see notes).
- Pinning checked against the previous head: with `scan_turned.rs`/`scan_hidden.rs` from def62da22 and this PR's tests, `turned_hidden_rest::a_pass_that_stops_short_of_the_groove_floor_it_entered_convicts` FAILS ("z 35.5 r 6.3 ... rest: 0") and `turning_hidden_floor::a_finish_that_stops_short_of_the_groove_floor_is_refused` FAILS; the other tests stay green, as intended. Restored afterwards (no diff against the PR head).
- Scope as before: no new dependency, no process/build/.github files, no goldens or PNGs, decision record updated.

**Results merged with main (trial merge clean), run locally** (no runner used; the review ran in its own worktree)
- `camcraft-sim` full test run: 68 suites ok, 0 failed (`turned_hidden_rest` 5/5).
- `camcraft-app`: `turning_hidden_floor` 6/6; 45 suites (every `turning*`, `lathe*`, `verify`, `verify_arc_reading`, `turn_pivot`, `sim_lathe_body`, `posting`, `stock_source_verdict`): 315 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. A finish that rides over a groove mouth (path level with the recess but not entering it) now refuses where it passed before; the PR states this is deliberate. It errs toward refusing, which is the safe side.
2. Not exercised by me: boring / ID work with a hidden floor, undercut (dovetail) recesses, a turning spindle not along Z (judged without the excuse by design, so it can only refuse), the other kinds (chamfer, taper, multi-pass) on a grooved part, an MCP/CLI reproduction, the ui suites, and the full `gate quick` plan. The recess is read along the scan's Z column, so a radially hidden cavity is only as good as that column reading.
3. Pre-existing: stock left on a plain OD or end face is not judged by the envelope law (stock sim's job), so a profile that stops short of the whole shaft is not caught here.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
